open_points.subject: execute_function / ExecutionObservation.report
open_points.text: - execute_function: [BEHAVIOR] The parent MUST enforce from outside a wall deadline, the monotonic_ns reading taken when the environment starts plus bounds.wall_time_ms in nanoseconds and held in a local variable of execute_function only, after which — once a later monotonic_ns reading reaches it — it kills every process of the environment by sending SIGKILL, through a pidfd, to the environment's PID-namespace init, the child-pid bubblewrap reports on --info-fd — not to bubblewrap itself or its process group — and then waits for bubblewrap to exit. It MUST return judge_execution of an ExecutionObservation of what it saw — whether the deadline passed, whether the runner exited abnormally (killed by a signal, SIGXFSZ included, or a non-zero status), whether cleanup was confirmed, the elapsed wall_time_ms, the peak memory_bytes and the decoded report — with the output ports and the bounds.
open_points.other_text: - ExecutionObservation fields (exact, no others exist): timed_out: bool, exited_abnormally: bool, cleanup_confirmed: bool, wall_time_ms: int, memory_bytes: int, report: RunnerReport
open_points.question: How can execute_function construct the required ExecutionObservation and call judge_execution when no runner report was read; must report become RunnerReport | None, or must execute_function synthesize a specified RunnerReport?

open_points.subject: judge_execution / missing runner report
open_points.text: - judge_execution: [DETERMINISM_OR_ORDERING] When cleanup was confirmed the outcome is the first that holds, in this order of = models.SandboxOutcome: timeout when the deadline passed; resource_exhausted when the memory, process, scratch or output bound was hit; sandbox_violation when the report holds any trap hit, even if the code caught it and returned a conforming dict; crashed when the report says crashed, the runner exited abnormally, or no returned message was read; contract_violation when the returned value is not a dict with exactly the output ports, an output is not_representable, its JSON text does not give canonical JSON through canonical_bytes, or fit_port_value with bounds.output_bytes as size bound does not fit an output to its port; otherwise succeeded. The stored value and spool ceilings are applied by the module that stores or spools an output.
open_points.other_text: - ExecutionObservation fields (exact, no others exist): timed_out: bool, exited_abnormally: bool, cleanup_confirmed: bool, wall_time_ms: int, memory_bytes: int, report: RunnerReport
open_points.question: How can judge_execution detect that no report message was read when observation.report is required and cannot be None; must the field be optional, or must the no-message condition be represented by a specified RunnerReport value?

open_points.subject: judge_execution output counting
open_points.text: - judge_execution: [BEHAVIOR] MUST decide from the observation alone and run nothing. The output count is the sum of the canonical bytes (from canonical_bytes) of every value output and the bytes of every file output, a many file output counting each element, compared with bounds.output_bytes; it decides whenever the outputs reach the parent, and output over a bound is a failure, never truncated. A bound counts as hit only when the parent observes it — the report's resource_hit or that count over bounds.output_bytes; the parent kills an environment for its wall deadline alone (owner, 2026-10-06).
open_points.other_text: - ReturnedOutput fields (exact, no others exist): port: str, form: ReturnedForm, json_text: str | None, contents: tuple[bytes, ...]
open_points.question: For a ReturnedOutput whose form is json but whose permitted json_text value is None, canonical_bytes cannot be called with the declared str argument; must the model require json_text for json form, or must the counting rule exclude malformed value outputs before calling canonical_bytes?
